newsitem.title: USA: Philadelphia "house of horrors" killer scheduled for execution.
newsitem.headline: Philadelphia "house of horrors" killer scheduled for execution.

text.p: A convicted killer who chained and tortured six women in his basement, fed them human flesh and murdered two of them was scheduled to die Tuesday after spending nearly 10 years on death row.

Gary Heidnik, 53, of Philadelphia, was scheduled to die by lethal injection at 10 p.m. EDT at Rockview State Correctional Institute in Bellefonte, Pa. Heidnik was being held at a prison in Pittsburgh.
A spokesman in Gov. Tom Ridge's office said a decision was pending on a stay of execution after death penalty opponents filed papers last week to stop the execution.
Heidnik was convicted and given two death sentences in 1988 for murdering two women he had imprisoned in his north Philadelphia rowhouse.
If executed, he would become the third person executed in Pennsylvania since 1962 and the first in nearly two years.
At his conviction, Heidnik also was convicted on counts of kidnapping, rape, aggravated assault and involuntary deviate sexual intercourse.

Heidnik, whose residence was dubbed a "house of horrors" during his trial, kept six women in chains in his basement between November 1986 and March 1987. He was accused of dismembering the body of one woman who died of starvation and feeding some of her remains to the others.
Heidnik also killed a second woman by attaching live wires to her chains while she stood in a pit filled with water.
Police arrested Heidnik in March 1987 after one woman escaped and led them to his home.
Police found body parts in Heidnik's freezer that belonged to the woman he dismembered. The second murder victim's body was found dumped in a state forest in New Jersey.
The remaining three women were found alive.
